title: Greet and introduce yourself
task: Meet a visiting agronomist. Greet them and introduce yourself, your role and workplace in 3–4 sentences.
evidence: Greeting + name + role + workplace; intelligible without reading.

title: Introduce a colleague and ask how they are
task: Introduce your supervisor to a visitor, then ask the visitor how they are and respond.
evidence: Correct third-person introduction, 1 question and a suitable response.

title: Exchange names and contact information
task: Role-play registering a new supplier: ask their full name, spell your surname and exchange a phone number.
evidence: At least 3 relevant questions/answers; letters and digits understood.

title: Identify common farm objects
task: Look at 8 farm-object pictures and name them; identify 2 plurals.
evidence: At least 6/8 recognizable nouns; a/an and plural forms when relevant.

title: Describe a tool or animal simply
task: Choose 2 farm tools or animals and give 2 observable characteristics of each.
evidence: 4 meaningful descriptors attached to the correct objects.

title: Say where you and your farm are from
task: Tell a foreign visitor your country, state, town and farm location.
evidence: 4 intelligible location details in coherent sentences.

title: Locate tools and animals
task: Using a simple barn picture, ask 2 location questions and answer 4 location questions.
evidence: At least 3/4 locations described accurately.

title: Identify ownership of objects
task: Sort 5 equipment items by owner and explain who each belongs to.
evidence: At least 4/5 owner-object matches expressed clearly.

title: Describe actions happening now
task: Watch a 30-second farm video; say what 4 workers or machines are doing.
evidence: At least 3 accurate current-action statements.

title: Discuss likes and dislikes
task: Tell a new coworker 2 farm activities you enjoy and 2 you dislike; give one simple reason.
evidence: 4 preferences expressed understandably and 1 relevant reason.

title: Ask about time and price
task: At a farm shop, ask for the opening time and prices of 3 items, then repeat the prices.
evidence: Time plus at least 2/3 prices accurately exchanged.

title: Explain your daily work routine
task: Describe 5 actions from your normal workday in chronological order.
evidence: At least 4 routine actions, including a time or sequence marker.

title: Discuss family and farm roles
task: Describe 3 family members or colleagues and explain each person's role in the farm business.
evidence: 3 persons and 3 roles clearly identified.

title: Describe farm facilities and layout
task: Using a farm map, describe 5 facilities and where 3 are located.
evidence: At least 4 facilities + 2 accurate spatial relationships.

title: Discuss weather and seasons
task: Read a 3-day forecast and tell a colleague the conditions and the safest day for outdoor work.
evidence: 3 weather details and 1 sensible day choice.

title: Order food or basic supplies
task: Role-play buying 3 items at a supply store; ask for quantity and total price.
evidence: At least 3 items ordered and one clarification question.

title: Describe abilities
task: Tell a farm manager 3 tasks you can do and 2 you cannot yet do.
evidence: 5 understandable ability statements with suitable verbs.

title: Describe past states
task: Compare the farm yesterday and today using 4 facts about weather, workers or equipment.
evidence: At least 3 appropriate was/were statements.

title: Describe your last working weekend
task: Tell a colleague what you did on your last working weekend in 5 steps.
evidence: At least 4 completed actions with past-time reference.

title: Shop for farm supplies
task: Role-play purchasing fertilizer bags and gloves with a fixed budget; ask for quantities and prices.
evidence: Correctly communicate two quantities, two prices and purchase choice.

title: Describe personal protective equipment
task: Look at a worker image; describe 4 PPE items and identify one missing item.
evidence: At least 3 correct items and a clear missing-item statement.

title: Discuss hobbies and free time
task: Ask a coworker 3 leisure questions and explain your own 3 weekly habits.
evidence: 3 questions and 3 frequency statements understood.

title: Suggest simple farm tasks
task: Given a messy storeroom, make 3 practical suggestions to organize work.
evidence: 3 actionable suggestions, appropriately phrased.

title: Explain a simple farm procedure
task: Explain how to clean and store a hand tool in 4–6 ordered steps.
evidence: At least 4 logical, safe steps in sequence.

title: Describe work routines across seasons
task: Compare your routine during planting and harvest with at least 3 differences.
evidence: At least 3 clear contrasts including frequency or time.

title: Contrast current actions and habits
task: Look at an irrigation scene: explain 3 things happening now and 2 things normally done.
evidence: 3 current and 2 habitual actions distinguishable.

title: Discuss next-season plans
task: Present 4 planned activities for the next crop season and their intended timing.
evidence: 4 specific intentions with reasonable temporal order.

title: Describe plant or animal conditions
task: Inspect 2 plant photos and describe symptoms or healthy traits without diagnosing.
evidence: At least 4 accurate observations, distinguished from guesses.

title: Compare crops, fields or equipment
task: Compare 2 tractors or plots on cost, size, efficiency and one other criterion.
evidence: 4 meaningful comparisons supported by supplied facts.

title: Report completed agricultural activities
task: Explain last season's harvest using 5 supplied timeline events.
evidence: At least 4 ordered, intelligible past events.

title: Explain an interrupted activity
task: Describe 3 incidents: what people were doing when each unexpected event happened.
evidence: 3 coherent background/event relationships.

title: Give directions around a farm
task: Using a farm map, direct a visitor from the entrance to 2 destinations.
evidence: 2 navigable routes with landmarks and direction terms.

title: Make polite requests and offers
task: Role-play asking to borrow a moisture meter and offering help with loading.
evidence: One polite request, clarification and appropriate offer.

title: Explain safety rules
task: Brief a new employee on 5 safety rules for a sprayer-storage area.
evidence: 5 understandable rules; at least 2 prohibitions.

title: Discuss abilities and possibilities
task: During equipment planning, distinguish 3 confirmed operator skills from 2 possible options.
evidence: 3 ability claims plus 2 appropriately uncertain possibilities.

title: Describe a farm visited
task: Give a 60-second report on a farm visit: facilities, practices and impressions.
evidence: At least 5 linked facts in an intelligible report.

title: Discuss career experience
task: Interview a colleague about 3 work experiences, then summarize your own history.
evidence: 3 experience exchanges, with accurate time framing.

title: Report recent changes
task: Using a maintenance board, report 4 completed or pending tasks.
evidence: At least 3 accurate updates and pending/completed distinction.

title: Explain a farming process in detail
task: Explain soil sampling from choosing points through labeling samples.
evidence: At least 6 ordered stages with no crucial safety/quality omission.

title: Advise on a farm problem
task: A coworker reports yellowing leaves. Offer 3 reasonable next steps without claiming a diagnosis.
evidence: 3 distinct justified recommendations and appropriate caution.

title: Discuss future schedules and forecasts
task: Use a harvest calendar and weather chart to distinguish fixed activities and predictions.
evidence: 2 scheduled facts + 2 evidence-based predictions clearly separated.

title: Make promises and spontaneous decisions
task: In a role-play with a delayed delivery, react immediately and make 3 feasible commitments.
evidence: 3 appropriately phrased decisions/promises with responsibility.

title: Report an operational problem
task: Brief a manager on a malfunction: what happened, what has been done and what remains.
evidence: Timeline, action taken and unresolved issue all clear.

title: Explain why tools and actions are used
task: Explain the purposes of 5 pieces of farm equipment to a trainee.
evidence: At least 4/5 purposes correctly related to function.

title: Specify supply quantities
task: Check an inventory and tell the buyer what is sufficient, low or missing.
evidence: At least 5 accurate quantity statements using the inventory.

title: Describe agricultural landscapes
task: Describe a rural landscape photo, locating fields, roads, water and buildings.
evidence: At least 5 grounded features with 3 location relationships.

title: Compare agricultural practices
task: Compare two weed-control approaches using cost, labor, risk and efficiency data.
evidence: 4 evidence-based comparisons and one reasoned preference.

title: Narrate a farm incident
task: Tell the story of an irrigation failure using 6 event cards in order.
evidence: Clear beginning, complication, response and outcome.

title: Present career history clearly
task: Explain your professional timeline and 2 experiences relevant to a new role.
evidence: Past finished periods and current experience correctly distinguished.

title: Discuss agricultural trends
task: Use a 5-year rainfall or productivity chart to describe 3 continuing trends.
evidence: 3 chart-grounded trends with suitable duration expressions.

title: Present a project timeline
task: Present a 6-month rotation project, distinguishing ongoing activities and completion milestones.
evidence: 2 in-progress future activities and 2 deadlines accurately expressed.

title: Explain likely consequences
task: For 4 realistic field decisions, describe what will probably happen if conditions change.
evidence: At least 3 plausible if–result relationships.

title: Advise strongly and infer causes
task: Respond to a storage safety case; distinguish mandatory action, advice and possible cause.
evidence: 3 categories clearly distinguished with justification.

title: Explain obligations and permissions
resources: must/have to; allowed to; past forms
task: Compare 4 workplace rules for employees and contractors, including a rule that changed.
evidence: At least 4 correct obligations/permissions and a past–present contrast.

title: Explain earlier causes of a past event
task: Tell the story of a failed planting operation and what had happened before it.
evidence: At least 3 accurate prior-event links.

title: Report prices and technical advice
task: Read 3 messages from suppliers/consultants and brief your team without quoting verbatim.
evidence: 3 faithful reported messages including source and key fact.

title: Ask indirect professional questions
task: Interview a visiting buyer using 4 indirect questions about specifications and delivery.
evidence: At least 3 grammatically and pragmatically appropriate questions.

title: Define tools, roles and processes
task: Explain 5 agricultural terms to a non-specialist without using the target word itself.
evidence: 4/5 useful definitions using precise relative information.

title: Justify agricultural decisions
task: Recommend a cover crop in a short memo explaining the objective, rationale and expected result.
evidence: Clear decision, 2 reasons and an intended outcome.

title: Summarize a technical text
task: Read a 300-word extension note and give a 90-second briefing of its key recommendations.
evidence: Main purpose, 3 key points and no major distortion.

title: Discuss alternative past outcomes
task: Review 3 historical farm incidents and explain how different actions might have changed results.
evidence: 3 credible counterfactuals, correctly anchored in the past.

title: Infer causes of past problems
task: Given a crop-loss case with 4 clues, propose 3 hypotheses and rank their likelihood.
evidence: 3 evidence-linked hypotheses with appropriate uncertainty.

title: Describe processes objectively
task: Convert a 5-step produce-handling procedure into a factual inspection description.
evidence: At least 4 accurate passive/process statements with correct sequence.

title: Negotiate politely
task: Role-play a delivery dispute: request a change, offer a concession and confirm agreement.
evidence: Clear request, concession and mutually understandable outcome.

title: Debate an agricultural issue
task: Debate whether to adopt precision agriculture, responding to 2 counterarguments.
evidence: Position + 2 evidence-based reasons + respectful responses.

title: Discuss an article or documentary
task: After reading an agro case study, summarize its argument and discuss two implications.
evidence: Accurate summary, 2 relevant implications and one question.

title: Evaluate professional strengths
task: Recommend a candidate for farm supervisor using 3 experiences as evidence.
evidence: 3 strengths linked to concrete examples; balanced assessment.

title: Write a formal professional email
task: Write 130–170 words requesting a correction to a seed delivery invoice.
evidence: Clear subject/purpose, evidence, desired action and professional tone.

title: Solve a multifactor farm problem
task: Given rising irrigation costs, propose 3 solutions and compare trade-offs.
evidence: 3 options, benefits/risks and justified preferred solution.

title: Compare systems and technologies
task: Compare manual and mechanized harvesting from a supplied cost/output table.
evidence: At least 4 supported comparisons and one defensible recommendation.

title: Give a short technical presentation
task: Give a 3-minute presentation on a known farm practice and answer 2 questions.
evidence: Opening, 3 organized points, conclusion and answers understood.

title: Describe career ambitions
task: Explain a 3-year agribusiness career plan with 3 milestones and contingencies.
evidence: Clear goal, 3 timed steps and 1 alternative route.

title: Analyze extended past processes
task: Explain why a soil issue worsened before an intervention, based on a timeline.
evidence: Duration, prior activity and present or later impact accurately linked.

title: Negotiate with nuanced language
task: Negotiate a service contract renewal with 3 constraints and one non-negotiable point.
evidence: Priorities, trade-offs, conditional offers and clear agreement/impasse.

title: Forecast complex future operations
task: Present a 2-year irrigation expansion forecast with milestones and uncertainty.
evidence: 4 precise future milestones/activities and 2 risks distinguished.

title: Use emphasis deliberately
task: Rewrite 4 neutral risk statements for an executive briefing, then justify emphasis.
evidence: 3 effective emphatic revisions without changing meaning.

title: Report with advanced passive structures
task: Write a 120-word neutral audit update from disputed observations.
evidence: Facts vs reported claims distinguished; 3 accurate passive structures.

title: Express wishes and regrets with nuance
task: Reflect on a failed harvest decision: 2 regrets, 2 desired changes and lessons.
evidence: Past vs present wishes clearly distinguished with feasible lessons.

title: Condense technical writing
task: Reduce 5 verbose research sentences, preserving agent, chronology and meaning.
evidence: At least 4 concise, unambiguous rewrites.

title: Report nuanced exchanges
task: Summarize a 4-person planning meeting including warnings, objections and decisions.
evidence: Accurate speaker attribution, 4 positions and agreed actions.

title: Use natural agricultural collocations
task: Edit a 150-word report containing 10 awkward word combinations.
evidence: At least 8 natural corrections justified in context.

title: Critique research and proposals
task: Review a short field-trial proposal, identifying design flaws and practical improvements.
evidence: 2 methodological limitations, 2 fixes and qualified conclusion.

title: Present complex technical content
task: Deliver a 5-minute presentation about a farm investment, answer 3 challenging questions.
evidence: Coherent argument, evidence, time control and responsive Q&A.

title: Write a formal report or proposal
task: Draft a 350-word proposal for a field demonstration with budget, risks and indicators.
evidence: Purpose, method, costs, risks, indicators and actionable conclusion.

title: Interpret figurative business language
task: Explain 6 idioms from an agribusiness meeting and restate them in plain English.
evidence: At least 5 meanings accurate; knows when not to use them.

title: Argue persuasively and respond to objections
task: Defend a sustainability investment to a skeptical board; address 3 objections.
evidence: Clear thesis, quantified evidence and 3 substantive responses.

title: Interpret implied meaning
task: Read a policy excerpt and identify 3 implied concerns, citing text for each.
evidence: 3 defensible inferences with relevant evidence and caveats.

title: Handle delicate professional situations
task: Role-play telling a key supplier their quality has declined without damaging the relationship.
evidence: Firm concern, specific evidence, tactful request and clear follow-up.

title: Discuss ethical and strategic dilemmas
task: Discuss worker welfare versus cost pressure using an agricultural case and two stakeholders.
evidence: Multiple viewpoints, explicit trade-offs and nuanced judgment.

title: Model uncertain future scenarios
task: Present optimistic, baseline and adverse climate scenarios for a crop investment.
evidence: 3 distinct scenarios, assumptions, risks and adaptive actions.

title: Synthesize multiple information sources
task: Combine a research abstract, market note and grower interview into a 200-word briefing.
evidence: 3 sources integrated; agreements, tensions and limitations identified.

title: Facilitate a technical meeting
task: Lead a 10-minute mock crop-planning meeting with conflicting priorities.
evidence: Agenda, balanced participation, decisions, owners and recap.

title: Interpret humor and irony appropriately
task: Analyze 3 ambiguous meeting remarks; explain literal and intended meaning and safe responses.
evidence: At least 2 correct interpretations; culturally sensitive responses.

title: Write an executive summary
task: Write a 180–220-word executive summary of a two-page agribusiness proposal.
evidence: Problem, evidence, alternatives, recommendation and risks, no filler.

title: Negotiate contract terms
task: Negotiate pricing, delivery, quality tolerances and penalties using a draft supply contract.
evidence: 4 clauses discussed precisely; clear concessions and final terms.

title: Mediate across languages and cultures
task: Mediate a 3-party misunderstanding between producer, foreign buyer and technician.
evidence: Accurate two-way paraphrases, confirmed understanding and agreed next action.
